sections.overview: The bare-nosed wombat is a burrowing marsupial native to southeastern Australia and Tasmania.
sections.identification: Its broad, naked nose and coarse coat distinguish it from hairy-nosed wombats in the genus Lasiorhinus.
sections.habitat: It occupies forest, woodland, heath and grassland; it shelters in burrows dug in well-drained ground.
sections.diet: It grazes mainly on native grasses, sedges and some roots.
sections.behavior: It stays in burrows by day, sometimes sharing them with other wombats.
sections.reproduction: A female usually gives birth to one young, which remains in her backward-facing pouch for about seven to ten months.
sections.ecology: Its extensive burrows provide shelter and are an important part of its way of life.
sections.conservation: The species is listed as Least Concern globally, although mange and road collisions affect populations.
